chunks: And from him, from al-Hasan, from Hammad, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Basir, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If you miss something of the voluntary prayers of the day and night, make it up at the time of the sun's declination (Dhuhr time) and after Dhuhr at Asr time, and after Maghrib, and after 'Atamah (late night), and from the end of Sahar (pre-dawn time).'

key_terms.السَّحَرِ: Pre-dawn time (last third of the night)
key_terms.الْعَتَمَةِ: Late night (time between Maghrib and Isha or late night period)
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: Declination of the sun (time for Dhuhr)

ai.seo_question: When should missed voluntary prayers be made up according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines the specific windows for making up missed voluntary (nafl) prayers, prescribing that they be performed immediately following the times of the corresponding obligatory prayers—Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, 'Atamah, and the end of Sahar. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that nafl prayers are generally linked to their obligatory counterparts, ensuring that the spiritual discipline of daily worship is maintained even when specific times are missed.
